answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days and the line already at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, any supplier switch (memory_c2) carries onboarding and continuity risk that could jeopardize scheduled deliveries—an unacceptable trade given the tight capacity margin. Memory_c4 shows that renegotiating with the incumbent at renewal previously recovered real margin and improved payment terms without any integration disruption, and memory_c1/c6 confirm the incumbent relationship has been stable and can yield further discounts via longer commitments. Given finance's 18% spend-cut mandate must be balanced against zero delivery slack, negotiating harder terms with the incumbent (leveraging market benchmarking and possibly a multi-year commitment per c6) offers the best near-term TCO reduction without introducing new supply risk. I verified c4 and c2 to confirm the actual conditions and outcomes behind these prior lessons before ruling out a vendor switch this cycle. This does not fully guarantee the 18% target is met—if negotiation falls short, a second-source or vendor switch may need revisiting next review cycle.
